recipes.name: Risotto with Chicken and Asparagus
ingredients_raw: 2 (5 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cubed
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring chicken stock to a boil in a small saucepan, then keep warm over low heat.

Heat 1 teaspoon olive oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Stir in the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the cubed chicken, and continue cooking until firm and lightly browned; set aside.

Heat remaining 2 teaspoons olive oil in the saucepan and cook onions until they soften and turn translucent, about 1 minute. Stir in the rice, and continue cooking until the rice turns opaque, and the onion begins to brown.

Stir in the wine and asparagus; cook, stirring constantly, until the wine evaporates. Reduce heat to medium, and stir in 1/3 of the hot chicken stock. Cook, stirring constantly, until all of the liquid has been absorbed, 8 to 10 minutes.

Stir in another 1/3 of the chicken stock and continue cooking and stirring until absorbed, 8 to 10 minutes. Season the risotto with oregano and basil. Pour in the remaining stock, and stir until absorbed again, 8 to 10 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper, then stir in the Parmesan cheese and chicken cubes.

raw_recipe.headline: Risotto with Chicken and Asparagus
raw_recipe.description: A delicious, authentic-tasting Italian risotto with chicken and asparagus. Perfect with a glass of Italian wine!

review.reviewBody:
This recipe turned out very well with some minor alterations: 
1) I used slightly more liquid than specified in the recipe, I believe about another half-cup of water to get the rice tender. 
2) I did not add the asparagus until about 7 minutes before I pulled the risotto off of the heat. The asparagus had time to cook adequately without going limp, adding a nice counterpoint to the soft texture of the risotto. 
3) This is not a recipe for 2 servings. This recipe had no problem feeding 3 people for dinner and two more for lunch the next day.
Was so good! Eaten up pretty fast. We added mushrooms and finished with extra butter and parmesan at the end for added creaminess.

Made correctly this is beyond a 5 star recipe--I used approximately 5 cups of chicken broth and skipped the Parmesan cheese (was out). Incredibly delicious! I diced the asparagus stalks but left the tips in tact (added the tips during the last round of broth). Will definitely make again!

This is a bit time consuming but it was delicious. I upped the wine to 3/4 c. as suggested by another reviewer. The only things I did differently were: I used fresh basil only because I happened to have it. I also used half chicken broth and half vegetable broth because I didn't have enough chicken. It wasn't dry at all like some of the others said. The consistency was just right, slightly al dente. I also did NOT put the asparagus in until the last maybe 8-10 minutes, which was perfect. It had a slight crunch.

This dish was really good, my picky italian father who makes risotto all the time even liked it... i made some changes, I added in mushrooms with the juice, as like the other readers said it was a little dry, definitely recommend adding more chicken broth, I also added saffron for my flavor and color. Instead of adding the chicken in at the end, I added it in in the middle as it looked like the chicken was getting dry as well. Will definitely make again, might try just mushrooms and asparagus and make it a side dish

Very Good. I roughly doubled the recipe, and it was enough to feed six comfortably. I decided to use chicken thighs instead of breasts because I think they have a little more flavor. Like many others, I definitely needed more stock and wine than the recipe called for. I followed the advice of many reviewers and added the asparagus closer to the end of cooking, giving it a little more crunch. I also decided to add the juice of a little less than half a lemon a few minutes before serving and it added a really nice flavor to it. I would definitely make this again.

Being the first day of Spring I was excited to make something with asparagus. I used Champagne instead of white wine. I used left-over chicken. I am not a fan of mushy asparagus so I cooked it seperately and then stirred it in with the chicken. The amount of liquid and timing on this was spot on for me. This was good for me but I guess the rest of the family is not a fan of risotto. They didn't get the whole creaminess thing. More for me. :)

Yum - I loved this!! I had to add a little more chicken stock at the end and keep cooking because though all the liquid would absorb, the rice was still a little too al dente - but that worked perfectly.

Very good. I skipped white wine (as I usually do onbthese receipes), used chicken theighs as that is what I had around and added a little more asparagus. I had to use a bit more chicken stock to compensate for lack of dine, but came out fantastic! Will make again.

This recipe required 3 plus cups of chicken stock, not 2. I am not sure about the oregano and basil. I would use this base but use thyme and maybe saffron instead. I now remember why I stopped making risotto decades ago! So much stirring!!!

Yum. I added a little poultry seasoning to the chicken to add a little flavor, as chicken can get bland at times. Next time I would use 1/2 to 3/4 c wine. I think I used a bit too much. I also used one quart of chicken broth (like I always do when making risotto), adding one ladel-full at a time. Like many other people, I didn't add my asparagus until the last 10 minutes or so. This turned out really nice.
It was ok. Really heavy
Yum! Added a bit of salt free seasoning with lemon to give it a bit of brightness. So good. I’d attach a picture, but all you’d get is empty bowls!
I had to use way more chicken stock. It took forever to cook. It never quite got the creaminess of risotto. I stirred and stirred. I will not make this again.
Delicious- I added fresh parsley and basil at the end. Just be patient as it takes a while for the risotto to plump up and be tender but it's really good and a nice change!
More rice and more wine
easy to make taste very good
took forever to make. flavor of the meal wasn't worth the time spent on it
This was amazing!!!! I loved all the flavors!! I followed the recipe but cooked everything separate then added it all together.. just added a pinch of salt! Simply delightful! This is a new favorite!
Loved it. Easy to follow recipe. Be prepared to put in the time but that is a given with Risotto. Well worth it.
